source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
source.citation: Toru Koizumi, Toshiki Maekawa, Masanari Mizuno, Maru Kuroki, Tomoaki Tsumura, and Ryota Shioya. 2025. RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables. In Proceedings of the 6th Championship Branch Prediction (CBP 2025)

summary: Exploits correlations between register values and branch outcomes by maintaining a Tomasulo-like table of recent register values. It computes a 12-bit digest of each value based on its format (INT, FP, Flag) and uses the digest of the most useful available register within each of 8 banks to index into weight tables for statistical branch correction.

state.name: sr_reg_digest_table
state.organization: Flat array with one entry per logical register
state.entry_format: valid (1 bit), payload (14 bits, holding ROB index when invalid or 12-bit digest when valid), decay_ctr (decay_ctr_bits)

state.name: sr_ut0
state.organization: Flat array indexed by logical register, then by hashed PC
state.indexing: logical register id and hashed PC

state.indexing: logical register id and hashed PC

state.organization: Flat array indexed by logical register, then by hashed PC
state.indexing: logical register id and hashed PC

state.name: sr_wt0

state.indexing: bank id and hash(PC, register digest)

state.name: sr_wt1
state.organization: Array indexed by bank, then by hashed PC and digest
state.indexing: bank id and hash(PC, register digest)

state.name: sr_wt2
state.organization: Array indexed by bank, then by hashed PC and digest
state.indexing: bank id and hash(PC, register digest)

state.name: sr_pred_state
state.organization: Queue with one entry per in-flight branch
state.entry_format: Per bank: selected_reg (7 bits), digest (12 bits), bank_was_useful (1 bit), avail_mask (9 bits)

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.pseudocode:
sR_total = 0
for b in range(num_banks):
    max_u = -999999
    best_r = -1
    avail_mask = 0
    for r in range(num_logical_regs):
        if (r % num_banks) == b:
            if sr_reg_digest_table[r].valid:
                avail_mask |= (1 << (r // num_banks))
                idx0 = hash(PC) % ut0_entries
                idx1 = hash(PC) % ut1_entries
                idx2 = hash(PC) % ut2_entries
                u_sum = sr_ut0[r][idx0] + sr_ut1[r][idx1] + sr_ut2[r][idx2]
                if u_sum > max_u:
                    max_u = u_sum
                    best_r = r

    bank_contrib = 0
    digest = 0
    bank_was_useful = 0
    if best_r != -1:
        digest = sr_reg_digest_table[best_r].payload & 0xFFF
        if max_u > 0:
            bank_was_useful = 1
            wt_idx0 = hash(PC, digest) % wt0_entries
            wt_idx1 = hash(PC, digest) % wt1_entries
            wt_idx2 = hash(PC, digest) % wt2_entries
            w_sum = sr_wt0[b][wt_idx0] + sr_wt1[b][wt_idx1] + sr_wt2[b][wt_idx2]
            bank_contrib = (w_sum * sr_useful_scale_num) // sr_useful_scale_den

    sr_pred_state[branch_id].bank[b].selected_reg = best_r
    sr_pred_state[branch_id].bank[b].digest = digest
    sr_pred_state[branch_id].bank[b].bank_was_useful = bank_was_useful
    sr_pred_state[branch_id].bank[b].avail_mask = avail_mask
    sR_total += bank_contrib

return sR_total

algorithms.name: allocate_dest_reg
decay_tick
complete_dest_reg
update
algorithms.pseudocode:
for b in range(num_banks):
    state = sr_pred_state[branch_id].bank[b]
    
    avail = []
    for r in range(num_logical_regs):
        if (r % num_banks) == b and (state.avail_mask & (1 << (r // num_banks))):
            avail.append(r)
            
    if len(avail) > 0:
        r_ut = random_choice(avail)
        idx0 = hash(PC) % ut0_entries
        idx1 = hash(PC) % ut1_entries
        idx2 = hash(PC) % ut2_entries
        delta_u = 1 if branch_prediction_correct else -1
        sr_ut0[r_ut][idx0] = saturate_add(sr_ut0[r_ut][idx0], delta_u)
        sr_ut1[r_ut][idx1] = saturate_add(sr_ut1[r_ut][idx1], delta_u)
        sr_ut2[r_ut][idx2] = saturate_add(sr_ut2[r_ut][idx2], delta_u)
        
    if state.selected_reg != -1:
        if not branch_prediction_correct or abs(LSUM) < theta:
            wt_idx0 = hash(PC, state.digest) % wt0_entries
            wt_idx1 = hash(PC, state.digest) % wt1_entries
            wt_idx2 = hash(PC, state.digest) % wt2_entries
            delta_w = 1 if branch_taken else -1
            sr_wt0[b][wt_idx0] = saturate_add(sr_wt0[b][wt_idx0], delta_w)
            sr_wt1[b][wt_idx1] = saturate_add(sr_wt1[b][wt_idx1], delta_w)
            sr_wt2[b][wt_idx2] = saturate_add(sr_wt2[b][wt_idx2], delta_w)

host_interfaces.need: Logical destination registers and ROB index at decode
host_interfaces.description: To allocate an entry in the register digest table, tracking in-flight producers.

host_interfaces.description: To generate the digest and write it to the digest table.
host_interfaces.fallback: Treat all completed values uniformly as INT.

host_interfaces.description: To unwind pending writes in the register digest table.
host_interfaces.fallback: Flush the entire register digest table on squash.

host_interfaces.need: Branch outcome, global prediction correctness, and LSUM magnitude at commit
host_interfaces.description: To apply learning rules to the WT and UT arrays.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: WT: 43008 bits. UT: 9360 bits. Reg digest table: 1495 bits. Prediction state snapshot (sr_pred_state): 29696 bits.
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: The paper states the register components cost 53863 bits (Table 3), matching exactly our WT (43008), UT (9360), and digest table (1495). It omits the storage of which registers were available and selected at prediction time, which the update path requires. We have explicitly added `sr_pred_state` to hold this snapshot (29696 bits for 128 in-flight branches), pushing our total 29696 bits over the paper's figure.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: At iso-storage, other SC components or the TAGE tables would need to shrink.

unit_tests.name: Allocate dest reg invalidates digest
unit_tests.given: An instruction targeting register R is decoded. sr_reg_digest_table[R] currently has valid=1.
unit_tests.expect: allocate_dest_reg sets valid=0, sets payload to the incoming ROB index, and resets decay_ctr to decay_threshold.

unit_tests.name: INT digest correctly folds fields
unit_tests.given: Instruction completes with INT format, value=0x0F (trailing ones: 4, leading zeros: 60, LSBs: 15)
unit_tests.expect: complete_dest_reg calculates digest as (4 & 0x3F) ^ ((60 & 0x3F) << 3) ^ ((15 & 0x3F) << 6) = 4 ^ 480 ^ 960 = 1444 (0x5A4), and writes this to sr_reg_digest_table while setting valid=1.

unit_tests.name: Decay counter expiry
unit_tests.given: sr_reg_digest_table has an entry with valid=1 and decay_ctr=256. Subsequently, 256 instructions are decoded.
unit_tests.expect: decay_tick decrements decay_ctr 256 times sequentially until it hits 0, at which point the valid bit is cleared to 0.

unit_tests.name: Prediction utilizes most useful register and scales by parameter
unit_tests.given: In bank 0, register 0 is valid and has UT sum of 5. Register 8 is valid and has UT sum of -2. Register 0's digest maps to a WT sum of 10. No other valid registers exist.
unit_tests.expect: predict selects register 0 for bank 0. Because max usefulness (5) is positive, it computes a contribution of 10 * sr_useful_scale_num // sr_useful_scale_den, setting sr_pred_state for bank 0 with selected_reg=0 and digest, and adding the scaled contribution to the total.

unit_tests.name: Update randomly selects available register for UT
unit_tests.given: At commit time, sr_pred_state indicates bank 0 had available_mask=3 (meaning registers 0 and 8 were available).
unit_tests.expect: update randomly selects either 0 or 8, and applies saturate_add or saturate_sub to sr_ut0, sr_ut1, and sr_ut2 for the chosen register.

unit_tests.name: Squash recovery invalidates younger instructions
unit_tests.given: sr_reg_digest_table has invalid entries waiting for ROB indices 100 and 105. A squash occurs at ROB index 102.
unit_tests.expect: recovery leaves the payload for ROB index 100 alone, but clears the payload for 105 to 0 because it was squashed.

open_questions: Figure 6 (a) INT registers: Does the leading/trailing count saturate at 63, is it modulo 64, or does it count bits matching the MSB/LSB? Assumed: counts leading/trailing zeros or ones matching MSB/LSB, capped at 63 using `min()`.

Figure 6 (b) FP registers: Are the extracted fields right-aligned at bit 3 or bit 0? Assumed: right-aligned at bit 3. Also, how is format classification done? Assumed: based on decoded opcode type rather than dynamic value inspection.
Figure 5 (c) x0 or x2.5 multiplier: The wire selecting the multiplier is not labeled. Assumed: the multiplier is 2.5 when the bank's maximum usefulness sum is > 0, and 0 otherwise.

Mispredict recovery of the register digest table: The paper declines to define a specific recovery algorithm and leaves it for future work. Assumed policy: on squash, invalidate any entry whose recorded ROB index is younger than the squash, leaving its payload at 0. Alternative: checkpoint and restore the entire digest table on every branch.

UT update rule: The paper states it randomly selects one available register per bank to update its UT weights, but doesn't specify the polarity condition. Assumed: standard TAGE-SC-L usefulness (increment on correct prediction, decrement on incorrect prediction). Alternative: update based on whether this specific bank's WT output was correct.
